comments.text: the menu's entry, from the shell's restart after the title and after every event. Sets up the sound ($1E34) and the screen ($13FA) and CIA 1's port A for output, the keyboard's columns; then, if the shell's resume address is set ($085E not zero), carries on where the menu was when it last loaded something: after an event, or after the registration it sent the players to ($1359, $1382)
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004) while it unpacks; once it is done, the menu's own start-up
the packed file's header, read by the shell's unpacker before the menu's bytes replace it
the packed file's header, its fourth byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the operand of LDA #$00
the last byte of the packed file's header the shell's unpacker reads; here, the operand of STA $083D

the main menu: sets the resume address to itself, clears the screen and prints the seven options (the number of joysticks patched into the text at $1088, NO) over YES when the travelogue is off), then lets the player pick one ($1AFC, the last choice remembered in $083E) and goes to it through the table at $10DB

the menu's text for $139C: its screen address, then "1) COMPETE IN ALL THE EVENTS", "2) COMPETE IN SOME EVENTS", "3) COMPETE IN ONE EVENT", "4) PRACTICE ONE EVENT", "5) NUMBER OF JOYSTICKS: 2", "6) SEE WORLD RECORDS", "7) INCLUDE TRAVELOGUE: (YES)", the shared words reached with code 2
the digit of NUMBER OF JOYSTICKS, written here from $087D before the text is printed
with the travelogue off ($087F not zero), NO) is printed over the YES
text for $139C: "NO) " over the YES, at row 17, column 29
the pick: seven lines from Y = $56, starting at the last choice ($083E), then to the chosen option through the RTS
where each option goes, less one, for the RTS at $10DA: low bytes; compete in all $116D, some $1243, one $1140, practice $10FF, joysticks $10E9, world records $12E4, travelogue $10F4
the high bytes of the same seven addresses
option 5: one joystick or two ($087D, 1 and 2 swapped by EOR 3); back to the menu
option 7: the travelogue on or off ($087F, which the shell reads before each event); back to the menu

option 4, practice: every player's record gets the name CONTESTANT ($1641), the practice flag ($081D) is set and the number of players is one; the player picks an event ($15EB), the scores are cleared ($16DB) and the event loads ($1382). When it is over the practice flag and the number of players are cleared, so the next competition starts with the registration, and the menu comes back

option 3, compete in one event: the registration or its check ($1651), "COMPETE IN WHICH EVENT?", the players' order shuffled ($1A91), scores cleared, the event picked ($15FA) and loaded ($1382); after it, the results ($17D4)
text for $139C: "COMPETE IN WHICH EVENT?" at row 4, column 3, from the shared words; "WHICH EVENT?" from $114E is reused by the practice heading
the players' order shuffled, the scores cleared, the event picked and loaded, the results
option 1, compete in all the events: the registration or its check ($1651), then every event's bit set in the mask $089D-$089E

the competition, for the events whose bits are set in $089D-$089E (option 2 comes in here with its own): the players' order shuffled, and for each event in turn, its bit shifted out of the mask, the scores cleared ($16DB), the event loaded ($1382) and its results shown ($17D4); between events, the medal table ($14F1) and a new order. After the last event, the final standings

the final standings: the scores cleared, each player's total from the medals ($157C: five points a gold, three a silver, one a bronze) into the score, the players sorted by it ($1A4E), a cyan screen with "FINAL STANDINGS:", tune 18 ($1E71 with Y = 6), and the players shown one at a time from last to first, with pauses ($1228) whose lengths depend on the number of players; then the winner's ceremony ($184B) and the menu
text for $139C: "FINAL STANDINGS:" at row 12, column 3
tune 18, then the players from last to first, each on its own row from row 14, with the pauses from $1206 and $120D
the pause before the last-placed player is shown, by the number of players less one: units of 74 frames
the pause between players in the final standings, by the number of players (from $120E); $120D, the first byte, is also the first pause for eight players
waits for twice A frames, or less if the fire button is pressed; first waits for the fire button and the keys to be let go ($1B6C). The music plays only where the caller's loop plays it
waits for A times 74 frames, playing the music ($1EA2) twice a frame; A = 0 returns at once

option 2, compete in some events: the registration or its check, "SELECT THE EVENTS TO COMPETE IN", the eight events listed, DONE below them; each pick turns an event's bit in $089D-$089E on or off and lists it again white when chosen, black when not ($161B); DONE with at least one event chosen starts the competition ($1175), with none goes back to the menu
text for $139C: "SELECT THE EVENTS TO COMPETE IN" at row 4, column 3, from the shared words
the mask cleared, the events listed in black, DONE in yellow, and the picks among the nine lines: the eight events and DONE
text for $139C: "DONE" at row 22, column 5, in yellow
each pick: DONE (line 8) ends it; an event's line turns its bit over in $089D-$089E and is listed again in white if now chosen, black if not
each event's bit in $089D, weightlifting first (bit 7) to sumo (bit 0)
each event's bit in $089E: none for the eight events; the eight bits after them would serve events 8 to 15, which the game does not have

option 6, see world records: "WORLD RECORDS:" and, for each event, its name, a colon lined up by the padding at $1788, the record holder's name ($1476) and the record ($14E0), all from the shell's records at $0E00; then tune 19 ($1E71 with Y = 7) plays, over again each time it ends, until the fire button is pressed
text for $139C: "WORLD RECORDS:" at row 4, column 3, from the shared words
for each event: its name at row 7, column 3, two rows further for each, a colon after the padding, the holder and the record
the tune's loop: a frame, two music steps; fire ends it, the tune's end ($12 = $FF) starts it again

sends the players to the registration: the caller's return address, from the stack, becomes the shell's resume address ($085D-$085E), so the menu's entry carries on with the option after the registration ends ($3C12); then the registration ($3A1A)
"NEXT EVENT:" and the event's name ($148E), then a wait of 400 frames, eight seconds, or the fire button ($1216)
text for $139C: "NEXT EVENT:" at row 4, column 3
the event's name after "NEXT EVENT:", then the wait

loads the event in $081F: the "NEXT EVENT" wait ($1369), then the caller's return address, from the stack, saved as the shell's resume address, and the shell's load ($0903) with X = the event's number plus 4: the shell loads part X-1, the event's file. The shell then runs the event, and its restart reloads the menu, whose entry goes on after the caller's JSR

prints the text that follows the JSR: two bytes of screen address, then screen codes in the colour in $46, to a 0 byte; code 1 and two bytes move to a new screen address, code 2 and two bytes print the 0-ended text at that address and come back ($149E). Returns to the byte after the 0
reads the next byte of the text at $2C-$2D and steps the pointer on; Z set on the 0 that ends a text
the pointer stepped without a read (the JSR's return address, one short of the text)
prints a space at the screen position in $2E-$2F
an entry nothing calls: Y = 1, white, into the colour, then the character
the colour in Y kept in $46 for this and the following characters
puts the screen code in A at the screen position in $2E-$2F and the colour in $46 at the same place in colour RAM ($2F EOR $DC turns $04-$07 into $D8-$DB and back); the position steps on
the small square, character $D4, in light red (10), before a player's name
the menu's screen: blue background, then $13FF

the menu's screen with the background colour as it is: black border, yellow as the second shared colour, white for text ($46), multicolour text mode with the screen at $0400 and the character set at $2000, sprites off; colour RAM set to the background colour so empty cells show nothing, the screen cleared, white rows of characters $B9 at the top and $BA at the bottom, and a striped rule of character $BB across row 2, columns 3 to 36, its cells red and white in turn on the character's yellow
prints the record holder's name for the event in $081F: ten characters of its entry in the shell's records ($0E00 plus 20 times the event, $14D8)
prints X characters from the address in A (high) and Y (low)
prints the name of the event in $081F ($1491 takes X), through the pointers at $1700 and $1708, as a 0-ended text with $139C's codes ($14D2)
the text's address in A (high) and Y (low), then printed
a code byte in the text: 1 and two bytes a new screen address, 2 and two bytes a text printed from elsewhere, anything else a character
code 2: the current pointer kept on the stack, the other text printed ($14CE), the pointer back
the text's address into $2C-$2D, then printed
prints the text at $2C-$2D to its 0 byte, the codes included
where each event's entry starts in the shell's world records at $0E00: 20 bytes apart, ten of name, one spare, six of the record as shown and three of its value
prints the record for the event in $081F: the six characters at its entry plus 11

between events: each player's total from the medals ($157C), the players sorted by it ($1A4E), and a table with each player's name, country and golds, silvers, bronzes and total ($1524). The "NEXT EVENT" text is then printed above it
text for $139C: "COMPETITOR         G  S  B  TOTAL" at row 7, column 3
one row of the table for each player, from row 9: the name ($1549) and the medals ($1565)
the bullet ($13F4), then the player's name and country, 16 characters from the player's record ($0800 plus 32 times the player in $37), in white
a space, then the six characters of the player's score as the event wrote it
the player's golds, silvers and bronzes ($19-$1B of the record) as two-digit numbers, then the total ($16) with more space before it
each player's points into the low byte of the score ($16 of the record): five for each gold, three for each silver and one for each bronze; the higher bytes were cleared before ($16DB)
the total: two more spaces before the number
a space, then A (below 100) as two digits, the tens as a space when 0
for the player at place $3A in the results (Y): if the score is not 0 and the place is first, second or third, that medal is counted in the player's record ($19 + place) and its name printed ($15E5)
where GOLD, SILVER and BRONZE start: low bytes
their high bytes
"PRACTICE WHICH EVENT?", then the event picked ($15FA)
text for $139C: "PRACTICE " and "WHICH EVENT?" from the shared words, at row 4, column 3
lists the events ($1607) and lets the player pick one ($1AFA), which becomes the event to load ($081F) and the next pick's starting place ($083F)
lists the eight events, A) to H), in the colour in $46; returns X = the last event picked ($083F) and A = 7, the last line's number
one event's line, X = the event, two rows apart from row 6, column 5: its letter, ")", a space and its name
the name every player gets in practice: "CONTESTANT", then spaces to 16 characters; it fills the name, its spare byte and the country's five

before a competition: the medals cleared ($16C8); with no players registered, or after a practice, the registration ($1359, which comes back here when it is done); otherwise the list of players and "IS THIS CORRECT?" ($166C), and if the answer is no, the registration again
"IS THIS CORRECT?", A) YES and B) NO, and the players listed below from row 11; the answer ($1AF2) comes back in X, 0 for yes, with Z set
text for $139C: "IS THIS CORRECT?" at row 5, column 3
the two answers, then the players
text for $139C: "A)  YES" at row 7, column 5
B) NO, then the players listed below, each with the bullet, from row 11
text for $139C: "B)  NO" at row 9, column 5
the players' rows, then the pick between YES and NO
clears every player's golds, silvers and bronzes ($19-$1B of each record): the loop's offset runs through each record 32 bytes apart, and the carry from the last one adds one to the next round
clears every player's score: its three bytes of value ($16-$18) and its six characters ($10-$15) set to spaces, by the same loop
where each event's name starts: low bytes
the high bytes of the events' names, all in page $17

the eight events' names, each ended by 0: WEIGHT LIFTING, BARREL JUMPING, CLIFF DIVING, SLALOM SKIING, LOG ROLLING, BULL RIDING, CABER TOSS, SUMO WRESTLING; then "WORLD RECORD", at $177B, and " RECORD" from $1780
for each event, the spaces between its name's colon and the record holder in the world records

the words the texts share through code 2: GOLD, SILVER and BRONZE for the medals, ") COMPETE IN " ($17A3, with "COMPETE IN " from $17A5), "ONE EVENT" ($17B1, " EVENT" from $17B4), "ING CEREMONIES" ($17BB), "PRACTICE " ($17CA)

after an event: the players sorted by score ($1A4E), the scores' texts tidied ($18B6), the world record checked ($18F6), then a cyan screen, "CONTESTANTS        SCORE" and every player with score and, for the first three, a medal ($15BE); players with the same score share a place, and the next place skips as many; then the winner's ceremony ($184B) and the sound off
text for $139C: "CONTESTANTS        SCORE" at row 13, column 3
the shell's unpacker's copy loop has $1800 as a placeholder operand; here, the results' text
the results' rows, one for each player from row 15: place in $3A, players with the same score as the one before counted in $3B so the place after them moves on by all of them

the winner's ceremony: the flag of the country of the player in first place ($081C) drawn in the middle of the screen ($197F), about two seconds of it ($1870, 60 times round), then that country's anthem ($1E71); when it has ended, the fire button clears the screen

one frame of the flag's colours: at raster line $4D, a white background and the flag's own second colour ($40), at line $8D cyan and yellow again for the text; a music step after each. Goes round until the music has ended, then 61 times more, counted in $16; returns with $16 = 0, so the next call returns as soon as the music has ended
compares the score of the player at X with the next player's, 32 bytes on: Z set when the three bytes are equal
for each player: a score text ending in M (metres) gets the small m, character $B8, instead; a score of 0 is shown as " FAULT"

the best score of the event (the first player's after sorting) against the event's world record ($0E11 + $14D8): if it is as good or better, "NEW WORLD RECORD FOR" the event with the old record and the new ($1943), the player's name and score copied into the record ($0E00 + $14D8: 11 bytes of name, then the score's 6 characters and 3 of value), a short wait ($1216, 200 frames or fire), and the records saved to the disk ($0906). Practice and competition alike can set a record
"NEW WORLD RECORD FOR" and the event's name, the old record's holder and score, then "NEW RECORD:" (the new holder's are printed by the caller)
text for $139C: "NEW WORLD RECORD FOR " at row 5, column 3
the event's name, the old record's line
text for $139C: "OLD RECORD:" at row 7, column 3
the old record's holder and score
text for $139C: "NEW RECORD:" at row 9, column 3
the end of the new record's heading

draws the flag of country Y, ten cells by five, at row 5, column 15 of the screen and of colour RAM, copied from the registration's strips of flags ($19B9, 78 bytes from one row to the next), and sets the two shared multicolour colours from $1A36 ($D022 the low nibble, $D023 the high)
five rows of ten bytes from ($2C) to ($2E), the source stepping 78 bytes a row and the screen 40
for each country, where its flag's characters start in the strips (the low bytes), 0 for the two unused places in each row of eight; USA $26BB, then every 13 columns
the high bytes of the flags' character addresses, by country: $26 for the top band, $28 the middle, $2A the bottom
for each country, where its flag's colours start in the strips: low bytes
the high bytes of the flags' colour addresses, by country: $2C, $2D and $2F

for each country, its flag's two shared multicolour colours, the low nibble for $D022 and the high for $D023: blue and red for the top row of countries, yellow and red for the middle, light blue and yellow for the bottom; the same as the registration's raster interrupts give each row
sorts the players by score, highest first: each pair compared on the three bytes of value ($16-$18), and swapped ($1AAF) when the later one is higher
puts the players in a random order: each player's record swapped with a random one's ($1ACF)
swaps the records at X and Y, from where each starts up to byte $1C: the last three bytes of each 32 hold the shell's and the menu's own flags, which stay where they are
the RTS that ends the swap; the table read as $1AC6,Y with Y counting from 1 is the one at $1AC7
where each player's record starts in the $0800 page: 32 bytes apart
a random number below the number of players: the random byte with the number added until it carries

the random number generator: a shift of $08FD-$08FE with feedback from its own low bits, and a counter ($08FF) mixed in by EOR. The three bytes are the tail of the eighth player's record, which no record copy touches; $1BD9 calls it every frame
the pick between A) YES and B) NO: two lines from Y = $66
the pick from the list of events: lines from Y = $5E; A, the last line's number, from the caller

the menu cursor: a yellow arrow sprite ($1B81) at the line in $30, lines from 0 to A, starting at X; with ten lines or more they are one row apart, with fewer two. Up and down move it, repeating every 24 frames while held and wrapping round; fire picks the line. With the joystick still, a key picks a line at once: 1 to 9, or A to I (taken as 1 to 9). Returns the line in X
the keyboard: the key's character from $3B4A, letters moved down to the digits, then a line number if it is in range
waits until the fire button and every key have been let go for 15 frames in a row
the arrow sprite, shape $C4, yellow, at X = $35 and Y = $3E plus 8 or 16 for each line
a routine nothing calls: waits for everything to be let go ($1B6C), then for the fire button
80 times X, two screen rows for each line of a list: low bytes
80 times X: the high bytes
40 times Y, one screen row for each player: low bytes
40 times Y: the high bytes

waits for raster line 251 to come and go, stirs the random number generator ($1AD9), and reads both joysticks together; a reading counts ($36) only when it is the same as the frame before. Returns the fire bit, Z set while fire is pressed
waits for the raster line in A

Denmark's anthem, tune 17: rows of four bytes for the anthem player at $1EA2, a note for each of the three voices (an index into the table of notes at $1DC4, 0 for silence) and the row's length ($1E1C); a row starting with $FF ends the tune; 48 rows, 23 seconds
France's anthem, tune 1, 20 rows
the United States' anthem, tune 0, 26 rows: the Star-Spangled Banner, its first notes in voice 3, 25, 22, 18, 22, 25, 30, the G, E, C, E, G, high C of its opening
Great Britain's anthem, tune 2, 17 rows: voice 3 starts 25, 25, 27, 24, 25, 27, the G G A F# G A of God Save the Queen
the anthem player's notes: SID frequencies, low bytes, note 1 ($0470) up by a semitone a step to note 43; note 0 is silence
the anthem player's notes: SID frequencies, high bytes ($04 for note 1 up to $32 for note 43)
the length of a row, by the row's fourth byte, in steps of the anthem player (two a frame, a hundredth of a second each): 1 is 192, 2 96, 3 144, 4 48, 5 72, 8 24, 9 36, $C 16, $D 80

sets up the SID for the anthems: every register cleared, then each voice's attack and decay $21 and sustain and release $84, the pulse width $0400 and the volume 10; no tune playing ($12 = $FF) and the tune's pointer at the end marker of Great Britain's anthem, $1DC3
starts tune Y, a country's number ($1E8A gives its tune), unless a tune with a lower number is playing ($12): its pointer from the list at $32C0 and the row's time cleared

for each country, two times its tune's number in the list at $32C0. The two unused places at the end of the first row of eight serve tunes 18 (the final standings) and 19 (the world records), which $11CE and $133B start with Y = 6 and 7

one step of the anthem player, called twice a frame: nothing when no tune plays; while the row's time runs, the gates are let go for the last five steps; when it has run out, the next row: each voice's note from $1DC4-$1DF0 into the SID, the gates off and on again, pulse waves for voices 1 and 2 and a sawtooth for voice 3, and the row's length from $1E1C. A row starting with a byte of $80 or more ends the tune ($1F1F)
silences the three voices (their frequencies to 0) and marks no tune playing ($12 = $FF)

the registration: up to eight players, each typing a name and choosing a country from the flags. Clears its variables ($11-$49), draws the screen ($3F96), starts its raster interrupts ($3A87) and sprites ($3A39); then once a frame (when the interrupt sets bit 0 of $18): the flags drawn at their scroll ($3E0F), the sprites' colours and the choice ($3EFA), the next step of the registration ($3BE2) and the joystick ($3D59)
the registration's sprites: six on (the frame's four corners, doubled in size, and the two arrows), shapes $C5-$CA, the corners black, positions from $3A70
the sprites' positions, X and Y for sprites 0 to 7, then the high X bits ($D010): the corners round the flag in the middle, the arrows at the sides of the top row
the six sprites' shapes, $C5-$CA
stops CIA 1's interrupts and starts the raster interrupt at line 251, through the KERNAL's vector at $0314 ($3AAB)

the registration's raster interrupt, eight a frame: the one for the line in $19 (7 down to 0) is reached by RTS through the tables at $3AD4 and $3ADC, and the next line comes from $3ACC. Each band of flags gets a white background and its own two shared colours, the rows between them black; the one at line 251 and the one at line 120 play the music ($1EA2), the one at line 120 also counts the frame ($14-$15) and tells the main loop ($18)
the raster line of each interrupt, by $19: 251, 235, 192, 171, 128, 120, 108, 64
where each interrupt goes, less one, by $19: high bytes
line 251, the bottom of the screen: a music step
the end of every interrupt: the border black, the raster interrupt acknowledged, and back from the KERNAL's interrupt with the registers from the stack
line 64, the top band of flags: white background, blue and red as the shared colours
the lines between the bands: a black background
line 128, the middle band: white background, yellow as the first shared colour (the second stays red)
line 192, the bottom band: white background, light blue and yellow
line 120: the frame counter, the main loop's flag ($18) and a music step
clears the registration's variables, $11 to $49
reads the keyboard: the first key found down, row by row from the last, gives its character from $3B85 in A and in $23; $FF when no key is down
the key's place in the matrix, row times eight plus column
the value for $DC00 that selects each row of the keyboard
each column's bit, compared with the inverted reading of $DC01
the character of each key in the keyboard matrix, row by row: DEL and cursor right as 8 (delete), RETURN as $0D, the letters, digits, full stop and space as their ASCII codes, the rest $FF
reads the keyboard row selected by A: $FF if the joystick in port 1 is held (it shares the lines) or the reading changes when the row is let go

the registration's steps, by $22: 0 starts with no players; 1 shows the screen for the next player and turns on the two arrows; 2 takes the name ($3C19); 3 asks for the country ($3CBB); 4 is the choice of country, run by $3D59 and $3EFA; 5, after the eighth player or an empty name, lists the players and asks "IS THIS CORRECT?" ($166C): yes goes back to the menu, which carries on with the option that sent it here; no starts the registration again
a lone RTS nothing reaches

the name, a key at a time: a character key types its character at row 0, column 23 onwards, up to ten, but not the same key twice in a row without a frame of no key between; DEL takes the last one back, again after five frames when held; RETURN ends it ($3C58)
DEL: a space over the last character, and a wait of five frames before another
